body:
### Design note: skills as attachments, not injections The issue names the hard part correctly: the question is not whether we can read a skill file, it is when a skill earns its place in a run. This is the design that falls out of how CodeAF already works. **The one law: the conversation holds the shelf; the work carries the skills.** Skill bodies never load into the chat. Chat carries only a catalog: names, one-line docs, and cost cards, windowed to what is relevant right now, with search for the long tail. When work needs a skill, the skill is attached to the *task node* doing the work, where context is fresh, bounded, and disposable. If chat itself needs skilled work done, it hands that piece to a quick task with the skill attached and keeps only the result. The conversation stays clean enough to think. **A skill here is five things, not one file:** 1. **Trigger** — cues and a one-line doc, what selection matches on. 2. **Payload** — the body, scripts, and resources, stored content-addressed and pinned by digest, so a rerun next month uses the exact skill that ran today. 3. **Check** — an executable "was this applied correctly," where one can be written. Attaching a skill attaches its check to the node's acceptance checks. Skill use becomes verified, not assumed. 4. **Cost card** — what it costs to read, to run, or to delegate, learned from real runs. 5. **Trust level** — authored, imported (provisional until it passes a trial in a clean workspace), or forged (distilled from repeated real jobs, arriving pre-trialed). **Attachment is per node, several at a time, ordered.** Real work is compositional: the render leaf of a task graph gets the video skill, the copy leaf gets the brand skill, and order is precedence. A skill can always be pinned ("use the pdf skill"), retrieval proposes from cues and scope, and a worker can pull a skill itself mid-run when it discovers the need. Pinned always outranks retrieved. **Three ways a skill is consumed, chosen by its cost card:** - **Read** — the body is pulled into the worker on demand. Cheap skills. - **Run** — the skill is an executable on PATH. Zero prompt tokens at all. - **Delegate** — the skill is itself a task shape; it runs as a sub-task and only the distilled result returns. Heavy pipelines, and the only way chat ever touches a non-trivial skill. **What keeps it honest:** every run records cost and check outcomes per attached skill. Skills whose attachments keep failing checks get rewritten. Skills that show no marginal value against similar runs without them are demoted to pin-only. Misses (a run that should have used a skill and didn't) write their cues back, so selection improves from real use. And a skill's check runs only when its payload was actually consumed; bodies are served from the store, so consumption is a fact, not a report. An attached-but-unused skill costs one doc line, nothing more. ```mermaid flowchart TD A["You ask for something"] --> C{"Chat (sees the shelf,
never the bodies)"} C -->|"pocket-sized step"| C2["Chat does it inline"] C -->|"everything else"| N["Task node,
skills attached by digest"] P["You pin a skill"] -. "always wins" .-> N R["Retrieval on cues + scope"] -. "proposes" .-> N N --> M{"Each attached skill is consumed by"} M -->|"read"| M1["Body pulled in on demand"] M -->|"run"| M2["Executable on PATH"] M -->|"delegate"| M3["Runs as a sub-task,
only the result returns"] M1 --> K["Node checks: the task's own
+ every consumed skill's"] M2 --> K M3 --> K K --> L[("Ledger: cost, pass/fail,
marginal value")] L -->|"earns its tokens"| U["Attached more readily"] L -->|"no marginal value"| D["Demoted to pin-only"] L -->|"misses"| W["Cue write-back,
selection improves"] ``` **What this means for skills written for other harnesses:** they stay where they are. The standard folders and formats are read unmodified, an imported skill works immediately at provisional trust, and it earns full trust by passing a trial rather than by assertion. Because bodies only ever enter disposable task contexts, imported skills get the same sandboxing as everything else the system runs. A skill collection becomes more valuable here, not merely compatible. **Position on the open questions in the issue:** - *Which folders and formats on day one:* the standard skill folders other harnesses read, unmodified. - *How a skill gets chosen:* pin > retrieval > worker self-serve, with the cost card and the ledger deciding how readily each is offered, and the shelf always visible for override. - *Many skills on one folder:* the catalog is windowed by scope and relevance; a folder's skills are candidates for attachment, never a bulk load. - *Showing cost:* the cost card sits on every skill row, and the ledger shows what each attached skill actually cost the run. Build order follows the loop: shelf and attachment first, checks and the ledger next, forge last. drafted with [CodeAF](https://agentfield.ai/github?utm_source=github&utm_medium=comment&utm_campaign=drafted_with)

## Summary

- The five-part skill record lives in internal/store and internal/resident: trust, cost-card and digest fields, and serving that marks consumption.
- Ordered per-node skill attachment on briefs: every briefed plan leaf now carries an ordered Skills list on plan.Node and on the journaled store.NodeBrief, composed at brief time by plan.ComposeSkills with pinned skills (names the person's proposal text says outright) first and deterministic cue/scope retrieval behind them. Function words never count as cues, one shared doc word is coincidence, three candidates at most.
- The worker's brief renders the attachment through plan.RenderSkillsBlock beside the working method; a leaf with nothing attached renders byte for byte what it rendered before.
- A windowed chat skill catalog (eight lines, scored, overflow line) and the depth-gated use_skill tool (list and get) are on the session belt wherever a store exists.
- Live wiring of NodeBrief.Skills: the chat engine reads the active shelf once per build, hands it to plan.Build frozen at both brief-journaling sites (the main plan and the remainder replan), and each dispatched leaf carries its plan node's attachment onto the task that runs it.

## Design

- https://github.com/Agent-Field/CodeAF/issues/1277#issuecomment-5753795826

## Test state

- `go build ./...` - clean.
- `go test ./internal/plan/... ./internal/orchestrate/... ./internal/session/... ./internal/store/... ./internal/resident/... -count=1 -timeout 30m` - all ok: plan 1.208s, orchestrate 0.598s, session 272.439s, store 14.302s, resident 17.970s.
- `go test ./internal/exec/ -count=1 -timeout 20m` - ok, 259.328s (added beyond the list above because internal/exec/linear.go, the render site, changed).
- New tests cover: a proposal naming a skill attaches it pinned and first on every briefed leaf (checked against the journaled store event and the graph node); a proposal naming nothing attaches nothing; retrieved candidates follow pinned entries; retrieval ignores function words and caps at three; the worker brief renders the block in composed order and renders nothing new when nothing resolves.

## Notes

- Later tranches: checks-on-attach, cost-card learning, and the forge.
- Unrelated commits: origin/santos/dev..skills/tranche-1 carries 17 commits from the feat/1089-custom-connections wave that are not this tranche - the named/multiple custom connections work (#1089) with its task and merge commits, the fzf v2 fuzzy matcher wave, a settings-row inventory, the settings search box cursor fix, docs/test chores, and two poem-chapter commits. They were on the checkout's trunk history before the skills work started.
- RenderSkillsBlock and SkillEntry moved from internal/orchestrate to internal/plan, beside ComposeSkills: the executor cannot import orchestrate (orchestrate imports the subharness, which imports the executor), and the render had no live caller.
- The change entry in docs/changes/unreleased is added once the PR number exists: `make changelog-new PR=<n> KIND=changed SLUG=skills-tranche-1`.
- origin/skills/tranche-1 already exists and points at 3bec5413f, an older lineage this branch does not carry (4 commits behind, including "session: fix ActivateSkill test callers after the skills merge"); a push will need reconciliation, which is the author's call.

—
Drafted with [CodeAF](https://agentfield.ai/github?utm_source=github&utm_medium=pull_request&utm_campaign=drafted_with) · reviewed and owned by the author- Carried non-skill hunks, named for reviewers: `internal/session/task_run.go` (resumeTree canonicalizes the checkpoint dir; a legacy `/var` vs `/private/var` mismatch made a macOS test permanently red) and `questionlifecycle_test.go` / `task_rename_compat_test.go` (two time-bombed assertions that went red Sep 17 when the day-leading stamp law landed). Both were proven pre-existing by running against a pristine archive of the base.

body:
> CC [@ZeroPoint95](https://github.com/ZeroPoint95) take ?

@santoshkumarradha The grading/performance ledger stuff is cool but I don't know that it's worth the complexity. It's usually easier to just edit a skill if there is something wrong with it, unless you are in a situation where your agents need to absorb a lot of niche knowledge over time.

I think it's hard to find a real use case where you both need a self-evolving set of skills and have enough useful information to actually do the evolution in a productive way.

Basically I would suggest starting with a simpler implementation to achieve parity with other harnesses:
- Discover and index existing skills (from other harnesses) assuming they are [agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io/home) compatible.
- make it really easy to add new skills (via folder OR repo url)
- all skills are user-invokable at any time
- a subset of skills chosen by the user may be auto-invoked in scopes chosen by the user (global > project > session)
- skills can be invoked or auto-invoked anywhere - don't *require* delegating to a task, but you still can
- a `skills` tab in `settings` (or standalone) would be useful here

Anyways open to discussion as always :)
Gtg with me. Feel free to update issues sur. @ZeroPoint95

issue.body:
## What is asked

Get codeaf listed in [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), the CLI that installs Agent Skills (`SKILL.md` folders) into 78 coding agents. The upstream change is small: one entry in `src/agents.ts`, `'codeaf'` in the `AgentType` union in `src/types.ts`, then their `validate-agents.ts` and `sync-agents.ts` scripts (which regenerate the README table and the package keywords).

## Blocked on #1277 reaching a release

A listing claims that codeaf picks up what `npx skills` installs. On `dev`, and in every released build (v0.4.1 and earlier), that is false: nothing in `internal/session` reads a `SKILL.md`.

The reader is #1277 (Santosh). It is on `santos/dev2`: #1365 and #1382 merged there, and #1396 is open. `internal/skills` scans `.codeaf/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.cursor/skills` and `.gemini/skills` in both the project and the home directory. That covers both places `npx skills` writes for an agent like codeaf:

- a project install: `<project>/.agents/skills/<name>`
- a global install: `~/.agents/skills/<name>`

For an agent whose project folder is `.agents/skills` ("universal" upstream), `installer.ts` writes global installs to the shared `~/.agents/skills` and never links them into the agent's own `globalSkillsDir`.

So this issue does not build a loader. It opens the upstream pull request once #1277 is on `dev` and in a release.

## The entry, and why its global folder is `~/.agents/skills`

```ts
// src/agents.ts, beside the other *Home constants
const codeafHome = process.env.CODEAF_HOME?.trim() || join(home, '.codeaf');

codeaf: {
  name: 'codeaf',
  displayName: 'codeaf',
  skillsDir: '.agents/skills',
  globalSkillsDir: join(home, '.agents/skills'),
  detectInstalled: async () => existsSync(codeafHome),
},
```

The first draft had `globalSkillsDir: join(codeafHome, 'skills')`, which is codeaf's own skills folder in #1277. Two reasons to declare `~/.agents/skills` instead:

1. **It is where a global install actually goes.** The README table and `skills list -g` would otherwise show `~/.codeaf/skills/`, a folder `npx skills` never writes to for codeaf.
2. **`npx skills remove -g` deletes inside the declared folder without checking it.** For every agent it targets, `remove.ts` runs `rm -rf <globalSkillsDir>/<name>` without checking that the path is a skill. With no `-a`, it targets every agent in its table, installed or not. `~/.codeaf/skills` is also the resident's promoted-commands shelf (`store.SkillsRoot`), and `internal/exec` puts its `bin/` on `PATH`. So once codeaf is listed with that folder, anyone removing a skill named `bin`, or one that shares a name with a promoted command, deletes that folder under `~/.codeaf`, even if they installed the skill for a different agent. Declaring `~/.agents/skills` keeps `npx skills` out of `~/.codeaf` entirely. Cline and Dexto declare the same folder.

`skills add -g -a codeaf` then shows `~/.agents/skills`, and #1277's scan reads it.

## Acceptance, end to end, on a codeaf release that carries #1277

- In a project, `npx skills add <a public skill repo> -a codeaf -y` writes `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Then `codeaf` in that project offers the skill: it is in the `/skill` picker, and a turn can use it.
- The same works with `-g`: the skill lands in `~/.agents/skills/<name>`, and codeaf opened in any folder offers it.
- Neither install nor `npx skills remove -g` touches anything under `~/.codeaf`.
- Upstream's own gates are green: `validate-agents.ts`, `sync-agents.ts` (README table, agent count, discovery paths, package keyword), `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm type-check` and `pnpm test`.

## Notes

- Upstream has about 83 "add agent" pull requests open. The ones that merged recently (fx, Sarvam Code, Posit Assistant) took days to weeks, so the pull request can be opened as soon as the release exists.
- `skills use <pkg>@<skill>` launches only `claude`, `codex` and `sarvam-code` (`USE_AGENT_CONFIGS` in `src/use.ts`). codeaf can be added there later, once a skill prompt can be handed to `codeaf` on its command line the same way.

body:
Cross-link: #1399 opens the `npx skills` (vercel-labs/skills) listing for codeaf once this issue is in a release. That listing makes codeaf a "universal" agent there, so `npx skills` writes skills to `<project>/.agents/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`. The scan in `internal/skills` already reads both folders.

One thing relevant to codeaf's own folder: #1399 declares `~/.agents/skills` as codeaf's global folder upstream, not `~/.codeaf/skills`. Upstream's `skills remove -g` runs `rm -rf <globalSkillsDir>/<name>` for every agent in its table without checking that the path is a skill, and `~/.codeaf/skills` also holds the resident's `bin/` shelf.

issue.body:
Step 1 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`), as its first commit.

## What

`internal/skills` scans the skill folders other harnesses already use and returns one catalog. It reads them in place and never copies them.

- Eight folders, first under the project (the git root of where codeaf was opened, else the folder itself), then under the home directory: `.codeaf/skills`, `.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, `.gemini/skills`, `.opencode/skills`, `.goose/skills`.
- After those, within each scope: the skills of installed and enabled Claude Code plugins, then Codex's bundled skills (`.codex/skills/.system`).
- A skill is a direct child folder holding `SKILL.md`. A link to a folder counts. Nothing is walked deeper, so the resident's promoted commands in `~/.codeaf/skills` (no `SKILL.md`) are not seen.
- First seen wins a name. Every loser stays in the result marked shadowed, so "why is my skill not used" has an answer.
- Frontmatter is read leniently, per the agentskills.io client guide. A bad name or a name that differs from its folder loads with a warning. A missing name or description, or YAML that won't parse, is skipped with the reason. An unquoted description containing a colon is repaired.
- Each skill carries its size (the bytes of every file in its folder).

## Acceptance

The package is pure, so its tests run against fixture trees under `testdata/`:

- precedence across scopes and folders
- each skip and warning case
- links, including dangling ones
- plugin skills and Codex's bundled ones
- the OpenCode and Goose folders

`go test ./internal/skills` is green.

Carried over from #1396 (Santosh), with the two folders the plan adds.

issue.body:
Step 2 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`).

## What

- **Every discovered skill is a slash command by its own name.** Skills become a second, dynamic source of commands beside the fixed table in `internal/tui3/commands.go`. The picker under the draft ranks them among codeaf's own commands, and the dispatcher consults them after the fixed table.
- **`/<skill-name> [words]` sends the skill's body plus your words as the turn.** The transcript shows the line you typed, not the body. If the skill is already in this conversation's context, only your words are sent, and the skill is named as already loaded.
- **codeaf's own commands always win a name.** A skill named like one of them is reached with `/skill use <name> [words]`, which does exactly what its own slash would have done.
- A shadowed or skipped skill is not a command.

## Acceptance, end to end

Real binary in tmux, with a fixture skill `pdf-processing` in `~/.agents/skills` and a stub model that records its requests:

- Typing `/pdf` shows `pdf-processing` in the picker, with its description.
- `/pdf-processing extract the tables` draws that exact line in the transcript. The model's request carries the `SKILL.md` body and `extract the tables`.
- Sending `/pdf-processing again` in the same conversation sends only `again`.
- A fixture skill named `help` is not reachable as `/help` (codeaf's help opens). `/skill use help hi` sends that skill's body.
- The manual answers "how do I use a skill?" and names `/skill`. The command-table gate passes.

issue.body:
Step 3 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`).

## What

- **Where the choice is kept.** Three places hold the same two lists, `on: [names]` and `off: [names]`. The narrowest scope that names a skill wins; otherwise the skill is off. Every write goes through one engine door.

| Scope | Where |
| --- | --- |
| global | `~/.codeaf/skills.json` |
| project | `<project>/.codeaf/skills.json` |
| conversation | the conversation's `meta.json` |

- **Catalog.** Skills that are on are listed in `message[0]` (name, one-line description, size), beside the standing orders and folders. The catalog changes only when a setting changes or a folder is attached.
- **The `skill` tool.** Its `name` is constrained to the skills that are on. It returns the body wrapped as `<skill name="…" dir="…">…</skill>`, with the skill's bundled files listed. Relative paths resolve against `dir`, and the skill's folder is allow-listed for `read`.
- **Absent, not broken.** With no skill on, neither the catalog nor the tool exists.
- **Every pull is visible.** Each call draws its own transcript row naming the skill and its size, for example `used skill pdf-processing · 3.1 KB`. It is never folded into prose.
- **Loaded once.** A second pull of the same skill in one conversation returns a short "already loaded". Compaction keeps a loaded skill.
- **`allowed-tools` pre-approves nothing.**
- **Words.** `prompts/system.md` says what a skill is and when to open one. `docs/CHAT-V3.md`'s "dropped skills & rules" line is invalidated by this pull request's change entry.

## Acceptance, end to end

Real binary with a stub model:

- With `pdf-processing` turned on globally, the request's system prompt lists it, and the tools include `skill` with `pdf-processing` in its enum.
- When the stub calls `skill` with `pdf-processing`, the transcript draws `used skill pdf-processing ·` followed by its size. The tool result carries the body and the skill's `dir`.
- With nothing on, the request has no `skill` tool and no catalog section.
- A project `skills.json` turning the skill off overrides the global on. A conversation turning it on overrides the project off.
- The belt gate names `skill`. The manual answers "which skills can you use on your own?".

Step 4 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`).

## What

**A Skills tab in `/settings`, one row per discovered skill:**

- a mark when the skill lives in codeaf's own folder
- the name
- the size, in bytes and estimated tokens
- its state: `on here`, `on for this project`, `on globally`, `off`

A skill with a warning shows it dimly. A shadowed skill shows what owns its name. A skill declaring `allowed-tools` shows the list. The tab does not say which harness's folder a skill came from.

**Keys:** Enter cycles the row's state for this conversation. A second key sets it for the project or globally.

**Commands:** `/skill on <name>` and `/skill off <name>` take `--project` or `--global` (default: this conversation). They go through the same engine door as the tab. `/skills` opens the tab.

## Acceptance, end to end

Real binary in tmux with fixture skills:

- `/skills` opens the Skills tab listing every fixture skill with its size and state.
- Toggling a row globally writes `~/.codeaf/skills.json`, and the next request's catalog includes the skill.
- `/skill off pdf-processing --project` writes `<project>/.codeaf/skills.json`, and the next request's catalog drops it.
- The tab and `/skill` never disagree about a state.
- The manual answers "how do I turn a skill on for just this project?".

issue.body:
Step 5 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`).

## What

```
/skill add ~/some/folder                    copies it into ~/.codeaf/skills/<name>/
/skill add ~/some/folder --project          into <project>/.codeaf/skills/<name>/
/skill add https://github.com/o/r           clones, finds every SKILL.md, copies each
/skill add https://github.com/o/r/tree/main/skills/pdf   one folder out of a repo
```

- A URL is cloned to a temporary folder with the `git` on PATH, and the skills are copied out. Nothing in it is executed.
- A name already present asks before it is overwritten.
- `/skill remove <name>` removes only from codeaf's own folders, never from another harness's. It never touches a folder in `~/.codeaf/skills` that has no `SKILL.md`: the resident keeps `bin/` and its promoted commands there.

## Acceptance, end to end

Real binary in tmux, no network:

- `/skill add <fixture folder>` puts `~/.codeaf/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` on disk, and the skill appears in the picker and the Skills tab with the codeaf mark.
- `/skill add file:///…/bare.git` (a local bare repository holding two skills) copies both.
- A `…/tree/<ref>/<path>` URL copies only that folder.
- `/skill remove <name>` for a skill that lives only in `~/.claude/skills` is refused with a message naming where it lives. `~/.codeaf/skills/bin/` survives every remove.

Step 6 of #1277. It lands in the single pull request for #1277 (branch `feat/1277-skills`).

## What

- A task node renders its own system prompt, so it gets the same catalog and `skill` tool for its scope.
- `propose_task` gains an optional `skills` list that pins named skills into a node's brief, so the chat can hand skilled work to a task with the skill attached.
- A worker on the bash belt gets the catalog and reads `SKILL.md` with the shell it has.
- A skill pulled inside a task draws the same row on the task page, among that node's steps.

## Acceptance, end to end

With a stub model:

- `propose_task` with `skills: ["pdf-processing"]` produces a node whose first request carries that skill's body.
- A node with skills turned on in its scope has the `skill` tool.
- The task page shows `used skill pdf-processing ·` followed by its size among the node's steps.
- The bash-belt worker's page lists the catalog with each `SKILL.md` path.
- The `propose_task` schema and the manual describe `skills` with the same wording.

issue.body:
Skills (#1277), on top of #1410. It is based on `santos/dev2`, which already has Santosh's skills work: skills from other tools read in place, `/skill`, `use_skill`, and skills chosen per message. #1396 is still landing there. When #1410 merges and `santos/dev2` is deleted, GitHub retargets this pull request to `dev`.

**Draft. Do not merge before #1410.**

## What is in it now

- **`.opencode/skills` and `.goose/skills` are read too**, under the project and the home directory. #1277's day-one list names both. They rank after the other six folders, so an earlier folder's copy of a name wins and the later copy stays in the result, marked shadowed.
- A change entry.

## Checked

- `make pr-ready BASE=origin/santos/dev2`: exit 0.
- **Real binary, real model (`deepseek-v4-flash`), throwaway home, driven in tmux.** Four skills were placed:
  - with the `npx skills` CLI, patched with a codeaf entry (#1399): one in the project (`add -a codeaf`, lands in `.agents/skills`) and one global (`add -g -a codeaf`, lands in `~/.agents/skills`)
  - by hand: one in the project's `.opencode/skills` and one in the home's `.goose/skills`

  All four were listed in the `/skill` picker. Each was used by the model on its own, and each answer carried that skill's unique marker line. The global one went through `use_skill get`.
- **On `santos/dev2` as it stands, attaching from `/skill` does not work in the real binary.** Every row says `memory is off, so this cannot be attached` even with `memory.enabled` on. The picker asserts `SkillFacts` on the surface's memory seam, but the launch hands it the `v3Brain` adapter (`cmd/codeaf/chatv3.go`), which does not forward that method. The picker test passes only because its fake memory has the method. #1396 moves that read onto the session. I built #1396's head with this pull request's commit cherry-picked (it applies cleanly and `internal/skills` tests pass). There the warning is gone, `enter` attaches, and the turn shows `· skills · goose-honk, open-sesame, house-greeting`.

## Still to do here

- After #1396 lands in `santos/dev2`: rebase, and add OpenCode and Goose to its `skills-from-other-tools` manual page in the same commit.
- #1277's plan items that #1410 does not have: per-skill slash commands, `/skill add` and `/skill remove` from a folder or a git URL, and a Skills tab. The plan's per-scope on/off conflicts with #1410's choice by meaning, and needs Santosh's call first. The sub-issues #1404–#1408 are being re-scoped as gaps against #1410.

issue.title: santos/dev2 lands on dev: the worker harness as default, runs as work, skills from other harnesses, the chat as manager

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
Brings `santos/dev2` onto `dev`. dev is already merged in with a real merge commit, so this is a fast-forward: dev has nothing that dev2 lacks.

**Status: draft.** The review fixes listed under "Still landing" are going into dev2 now. This PR follows them automatically and goes ready when they are in.

## What this brings

**1. The worker harness, now the default.** A task runs on a bash belt: one loop under both `/task` and `codeaf do`, with a checking seat for the belt check. `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=node` (or `legacy`, or `off`) is the way back to the older node belt. See #1109 waves 1, 2, 6 and 7, and #1335, #1340, #1355, #1207.

**2. Runs as first-class work.**
- A run's life is the conversation's.
- It works in its own copy, and the copy is written down so it can be found again.
- Dollar and time limits end it by one road, and the ending names the limit that caused it.
- A run's dollars reach the conversation's total.
- Work that nothing is driving reads as interrupted, not failed, and can be carried on.
- A stopped task reads stopped everywhere.

About 50 entries, from #1204 through #1305.

**3. Skills, first design (to be replaced).** A memory-backed shelf, `use_skill`, per-message automatic choice, a `/skill` picker that attaches a skill, and a report of which skills a turn used (#1327, #1345–#1348, #1380). This follows the first design in #1277. #1409 builds the settled plan on dev and replaces these pieces after this lands; see the note on #1409.

**4. The chat as manager over the plan store.** The chat role. The chat sees the plan when the person speaks, and notes are a channel into a running worker. See #1205, #1354, #1356 and #1357.

**5. Task page, rail and step rows.** The page and rail door. Step rows are cut from the commands as they ran, step numbers continue across a wake, and a call that did not run has no row. See #1231, #1257, #1260 and #1261.

**6. Pickers.** One fuzzy matcher for every picker, match highlighting, and the caret parks where you type (#1321).

**7. Benchmarks and docs.** The footprint benchmark and its method, resume cost (#1126, #1317), and ADHD-shaped answers (#1209).

**8. Hardening.**
- Heavy-suite locks as kernel file locks (#1264, #1270, #1284, #1324).
- Goroutine ownership at close (#1259, #1267, #1274, #1276).
- Unread and retired profile keys (#1223, #1245).
- The CI gate on this branch (#1362).

## Behaviour that changes on merge

- **Tasks run on the bash belt by default.** Before, `CODEAF_TASK_BELT=bash` opted in. Now `node`, `legacy` or `off` opts out.
- `task.parallel` = 0 means no limit on both doors.

## Review

Every feature group above had a feature-level review against its change entry. The findings are being fixed in their own PRs into dev2, each with tests shown failing first and a full `make check` on the merged head.

Already in:
- #1411: run lifecycle (10 findings). A new request never adopts an earlier run, every ending is written on the root, the dollar limit ends peers, close lands nothing, steers on ended runs are refused, interrupted rows are honest.
- #1393: chat manager (9 findings). The digest leads with the live run in the rail's words, `say` and `forward` reach run rows, a key that is read is no longer reported unread, and `Assisted-by` follows `/model`.
- #1395: task page keys, the tab mark, pool judge sweep claims, unowned catalog warms, manual gaps (12 findings).
- The dev merge: a parked parent could wake before its child's review check was seated. Fixed in `internal/run`, 100 stress runs green.

Still landing:
- **`codeaf do`.** It must never commit work it did not make. Spend stays bounded unless the person says otherwise. Project `*.lock` files land.
- **Retry loop.** A server that keeps cutting its answer short is waited on, not re-asked in a tight loop. "One machine" applies only when routing is actually off.
- **Attribution.** Always on: every commit codeaf writes carries `Assisted-by: CodeAF (<model>)` then `Co-Authored-By`. The model is shown as its bare name, with no provider prefix, and it is the one part a person can turn off.

## Evidence

- The merge of dev into dev2 at `525b77fde`: full `make check` EXIT 0, including the Windows cross-builds. Nothing is on the known-red list.
- #1395 at `635c029c6`, #1393 at `449e7921c`, #1411 at `888911c05`: full `make check` EXIT 0 each. CI green on each.

issue.title: Skills from Claude Code plugins and Codex, with memory off, chosen by what they are for

repository.name: CodeAF
repository.description: Open-Source Software factory for Open Models

issue.body:
Skills installed for Claude Code and Codex now reach codeaf directly, with memory on or off, and the model picks the one a request fits by what the skill is for.

## What changed

- **Claude Code plugin skills are read**, the way Claude Code decides what is live: the plugin is named in `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json`, `enabledPlugins` says true in the layered settings (home, project, project local), and a project-scoped install counts only in its own project. A plugin reads the skill folders its manifest or its marketplace catalog entry names, and only those; a plugin that names none is read from `skills/`. The plugins folder is never walked, so marketplace clones and older cached versions are left alone. A plugin skill keeps its bare folder name, ranks below every hand-kept skill and above Codex's bundled ones; the decision is written up in `internal/skills/plugins.go`.
- **Codex's bundled skills** in `.codex/skills/.system` are read, below everything else in their scope.
- **Linked skill folders** are followed, which is how `npx skills` and similar installers reach every tool from one copy.
- **Memory off no longer turns skills off.** With `memory.enabled` off the process builds its shelf in a temporary store from the skill folders and removes it on close. Nothing is written to the memory store the person turned off. `use_skill`, the catalog and the per-message carry all work. The #1380 "switched off" line is gone.
- **The catalog lists every skill, by what it is for.** It is in the stable prefix in a fixed order: scope match first, then by name. The recency ordering is gone so the order cannot move between requests. Descriptions are clipped to 160 characters, and the described lines stop at 12 KiB. The names that did not fit follow on one line of up to 2 KiB, and anything past that is counted. The model opens the skill a request fits with `use_skill`. The word-match carry still runs first on every message.
- **The carried-skills line stays visible.** On the chat surface the line reads `skills · <names>`. Once the answer landed, the `▸ worked` chip swallowed it, and even an opened chip did not show it. It now stays under the message, with the chip starting below it.
- **The `/skill` picker and the attachment work on the ordinary launch.** The picker reads the conversation's own shelf. Attach, detach, list and clear cross the session-host connection (`remote.Agent` methods, `Welcome.Skills`, `serveSkills`), where they had been missing. `skillAttacher` leaves the surface-door ledger, and the ratchet is now 21 after the merge with the base's own removal.
- **The attachment is a fact and not a call.** `session.Facts.Skills` carries the attachment down unasked, and the engine announces it after every attach, detach or clear. The chip reads the replica, and the picker asks the shelf and the attachment doors off the update loop (the base's new off-loop laws).
- The shelf holds 400 skills (was 100).
- Manual: `skills-from-other-tools.md` (new), `use-skill.md`, `putting-a-skill-in-front.md`, `skills-a-turn-used.md`, `what-i-remember.md`; six new retrieval probes. Change entry `docs/changes/unreleased/1396-skills-from-other-tools.md`.

**Catalog cost:** each described line is `- name: description`, with the description clipped to 160 characters. That is about 120 to 230 bytes per skill, most often 150 to 180. It is paid once, in the cached prefix. The whole section is bounded at 12 KiB of described lines plus 2 KiB of names.

## Evidence (remote test box; every `go test` with `-count=1`)

- **Red first.** Each new unit test was run against the unfixed implementation with the new tests in place. skills: a compile red, then six assertion reds. resident: two assertion reds. session, tui3, remote and cmd/codeaf: compile reds. The plugin manifest test failed on the earlier discovery code. The carried-line test failed on the earlier feed and fold code.
- **End-to-end, the real binary in tmux, fresh home, both memory settings, on the head:** `TestTUIE2E/foreign_skills_reach_the_conversation` PASS for memory_on and memory_off. Three skills are installed: one in `.claude/skills`, one in `.codex/skills`, and one in an installed and enabled plugin. It asserts:
  - (a) automatic: `skills · tide-almanac` with `QUILLON-TIDE-7431`, then `skills · lantern-ledger` with `LANTERN-LEDGER-2958`;
  - (b) by hand: `/skill orchard` lists the plugin skill with no refusal, Enter attaches it, and a question sharing no words carries `skills · orchard-census` and answers with `ORCHARD-CENSUS-6612`;
  - (c) the transcript records `use_skill` with `"mode":"list"` and `"mode":"get"`.
- **Real installs in a fresh home.** Installed with `npx skills add` (one skill global for Claude Code, one project-level for Codex into `.agents/skills`), `claude plugin marketplace add` plus `claude plugin install example-skills@…` (Claude Code 2.1.278), `claude plugin init` (a skills-dir plugin), and a hand-written `~/.codex/skills` skill. `use_skill` list returned all 15 skills, memory off and memory on. The 12 plugin skills are exactly the set `claude plugin details` lists; the 7 other folders in the plugin's repository, which belong to other plugins, are not offered. A p5.js request opened the plugin's `algorithmic-art` skill, and a harbour-log request followed the Codex skill.
- **Relevance eval** (`TestSkillRelevanceEval`, deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, 12 paraphrases sharing almost no words with their skill plus 4 needing no skill, two runs per arm, each request in its own folder). Before is the base build 3f46952d4:

| arm | paraphrases reaching their skill | requests left alone |
|---|---|---|
| before, memory on | 12/24 | 8/8 |
| before, memory off | 0/24 | 8/8 |
| after, memory on | 16/24 | 8/8 |
| after, memory off | 15/24 | 8/8 |

- **Gate on the head 2f87cbc2e.** Build, vet (untagged and e2e) and `make changelog-check` are clean, and the touched light packages (skills, resident, remote, manual, e2e, store, cmd/codeaf) pass.
  - Full `make check` exits 2 and is **not green**. It failed in `internal/run` (TestNotesBeyondTheBoundWaitForTheNextBoundary: step cap), `internal/session` (TestHandingAYourCallToTheModelAndItsResolveAreOneRoad) and `internal/telemetry` (two spool tests).
  - None of these packages' code paths is touched here, and none of these tests failed in the previous full run on this branch. They have not been confirmed against the base.
  - `internal/tui3` passes in that run, including the off-loop laws.

**On hold** since 2026-09-23: #1409 carries the approved skills design, so this branch stops here until Santosh decides.

## Not reached yet

- Claude Code's `disable-model-invocation` and `user-invocable` frontmatter are not honoured; every skill is offered both ways.
- A `SKILL.md` deeper than a direct child of a skills folder is not read. A skills-dir plugin with only a nested `skills/` folder is not read either.
- `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocation is not followed.
- With `CODEAF_HOME` set, the user-scope folders are read under that folder, not `$HOME`. That is by design (`home.Login`).
- The picker discovers from the local disk even over `--host` to another machine.
- Task workers with memory off do not get the shelf through the executor's own store path.
